newsitem.title: FRANCE: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV FAILS IN WORLD RECORD BID.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV FAILS IN WORLD RECORD BID.

text.p: Double Olympic champion Denis Pankratov fell well short of his world record pretentions in the men's 200 metres butterfly at the Canet international meeting on Saturday.

The Russian announced before the meeting -- his last before the European championships in Seville in August -- that he was gunning for his own world record of one minute 55.22 seconds, but only managed 1:57.34.
Pankratov was inside world record time in the first three lengths but lost pace over the last 50 metres, a second disappointment this week after his sixth place in Barcelona in the 100 butterfly.
"Denis was not sufficiently concentrated," his coach Viktor Avdeienko said after the final.
He said that Pankratov would now continue his preparations for the August 18-24 European championships at home in Russia.

Costa Rica's Olympic champion Claudia Poll, in her first long-course competition of the season, won the women's 200 metres freestyle in a respectable time of 1:58.18 after only four weeks' training in a 50-metre pool.
